interpretationRules.shortQuote: Whenever a card fundamentally contradicts the rules, the card’s indication is what is true.
interpretationRules.conclusion: Card text can create a specific exception only for a fundamental contradiction; it is not a blanket numerical priority.

interpretationRules.shortQuote: Card text should be interpreted according to these rules, not as though it were text within these rules.
interpretationRules.conclusion: Card terms use the Core Rules definitions and do not automatically override definitions by sharing a word.

interpretationRules.shortQuote: Cards that forbid actions or effects, as a broad method of determination, supersede cards that allow or permit that same action or effect.
interpretationRules.conclusion: Apply the prohibition only to the same action or effect and under its concrete conditions; do not create one global source-order number.

interpretationRules.shortQuote: Game Actions cannot be performed simultaneously for any reason.
interpretationRules.conclusion: When simultaneous actions/effects/triggers are ordered, use the applicable turn-order/controller rule. This does not make every chain FIFO or LIFO and does not replace Finalize oldest-first plus Resolve newest-first.

effectOrderPolicy.sourcePrecedence: Use the applicable current Core Rules, effective card errata and official rulings for the concrete interaction. A newer Core Rules document supersedes conflicting official rulings; community FAQ/video is not authoritative.

entries.interaction: Player Priority/Focus and legal Reaction windows
timeline: Up to one player holds Priority and up to one player holds Focus.
A player who gains Focus also gains Priority; passing Priority does not pass Focus.
In a Closed State, only Reaction cards/abilities are legally timed.
A new Pending item restarts the Execute/Pass sequence and cannot be resolved with a stale pass count.
entries.playerChoiceWindow: The Priority holder chooses a legally timed card/ability or passes; Focus additionally governs Showdown discretionary actions.
entries.responseWindow: Reaction may be played during Closed States on any player turn and before the current spell/ability resolves.

entries.interaction: Cost choice, target/choice locking, atomic payment, legality and rollback
timeline: Make the card choices and add the item as Pending.
Determine the total cost in the CR 356 order, including chosen optional additions.
Pay Energy/Power and nonstandard costs in CR 357.
Check choices, payment, outcome and timing in CR 358.
If Finalize fails, undo the play and all actions caused by it.
entries.playerChoiceWindow: The playing controller chooses optional additions and legal choices before the applicable Finalize checks.
entries.responseWindow: A legally timed Reaction can be added while the item is Pending/Finalized; Finalizing itself does not pass Priority.

entries.interaction: Continuous layer order, object dependencies and dependency loops
timeline: Evaluate continuously, but pause a dependent object while referenced objects are evaluated.
Resolve a dependency chain from its far endpoint; evaluate a loop simultaneously layer by layer.
Apply copy, trait, ability and arithmetic layers in order.
Reapply layers until a fixed point and re-check conditions after changes.

entries.responseWindow: Players do not receive Priority merely because layers recompute; any new trigger follows its own trigger rules.

entries.interaction: Pending, Finalize, Priority/Pass and Resolve lifecycle
timeline: The played object/ability enters as a Pending Chain Item.
Finalize items oldest-first; Finalizing does not pass Priority.
Execute/Pass restarts whenever a new item is added.
After consecutive passes, the newest Finalized item resolves.
Priority then follows the remaining newest item; an empty Chain returns to an Open State.
entries.playerChoiceWindow: The Priority holder chooses to add a legally timed item or pass; the controller of each Pending item supplies required Finalize choices/costs.
entries.responseWindow: Reaction may be added during Closed State; Finalization does not itself open a Priority grant.

entries.sourceConflict: Finalize oldest-first and Resolve newest-first are distinct from CR 303.2.a ordering; the implementation must not flatten them into one FIFO/LIFO rule.

entries.interaction: Invalid targets, Ignored/Negated instructions, linked instructions and LKI
timeline: Lock choices/targets at Finalize and retain their incarnation information.

Read LKI only where a linked/zone-changing instruction authorizes it.
Skip later linked instructions only when the earlier linked instruction was Ignored or when “if you do” directly requires the action.
entries.playerChoiceWindow: Choices made after Finalize occur only where the rule text requires them; already locked costs/targets are not reselected.
entries.responseWindow: Opponents may change zones/target legality through legal Reactions before Resolve; Finalize locks do not bypass later rechecks.

timeline: Open Combat and perform start-of-combat effects.

Assign damage, then deal all assigned combat damage simultaneously.

source.title: Core Rules: Radiance Patch Notes (Effective October 16, 2026)
source.notes: Official rulings state that a later Core Rules document takes precedence over differing rulings.
source.relevantParagraph: Items cannot be placed on the chain simultaneously for any reason. Each player orders its own units; players place their groups in turn order; Pending items are finalized oldest-to-newest and units resolve as soon as finalized.

timeline: Chronobreak banishes selected units.
Each owner chooses the order of its own units played back.
Owners place their groups in turn order starting with the turn player.
Pending items are finalized oldest-to-newest; the applicable unit resolves when finalized.
After the group, play effects are finalized in the order they triggered; players may react to the most recent item.
entries.playerChoiceWindow: Each owner chooses only the order of its own units; no single player chooses all players’ units.
entries.responseWindow: Reactions occur only at the actual Chain window after the applicable items have been finalized; there is no invented global “simultaneous chain”.

entries.missingEvidence: Current program sourceText uses “uncontrolled” from RAD-181-167. The selected M1 printing sfd-233-star-221 and the official Spiritforged errata use “open”. The program must be reviewed against the selected printing/current errata by the existing card-dsl owner.

entries.interaction: Riposte Reaction, counter, linked printed-cost read and LKI
timeline: Riposte is played as a Reaction and becomes a Pending Chain Item.
At Finalize, lock the friendly unit and target spell; pay 2 Energy + 2 Power.
At Resolve, counter the spell and retain the printed Energy value needed by the linked instruction.
Register the Might modification for the chosen unit and expire it this turn.
entries.playerChoiceWindow: The Riposte controller chooses the friendly unit and the spell on the Chain; those choices lock at Finalize.
entries.responseWindow: Riposte is legally timed in a Closed State; opponents can respond before it resolves.
